fields.name: vehicle_id
fields.hint: the vehicle identifier on the Vehicle line, verbatim -- the VEH- code only, not the platform label

fields.name: coverage_plan
fields.hint: the coverage plan this claim is filed under, verbatim

fields.name: in_service_date
fields.hint: the date the vehicle went into service, YYYY-MM-DD, verbatim

fields.name: repair_date
fields.hint: the date the repair was performed, YYYY-MM-DD, verbatim

fields.name: months_in_service
fields.hint: COMPLETE months between in_service_date and repair_date, as a bare whole number. Compute it as (repair year - in-service year) x 12 + (repair month - in-service month), then subtract 1 if the repair day-of-month is EARLIER than the in-service day-of-month. A vehicle in service on the 18th is 35 months old on the 17th of the 36th month and 36 months old on the 18th

fields.name: odometer_miles
fields.hint: the odometer reading at the repair, as a bare number without the unit

fields.name: failed_component
fields.hint: the component the claim says failed, verbatim

fields.name: claimed_labor_op
fields.hint: the labor operation code claimed, verbatim

fields.name: cause_code
fields.hint: the CODED cause on the claim form, copied verbatim. This is what the dealer coded, which is not necessarily what the technician describes -- copy it, do not reason from it

fields.name: claim_status
fields.hint: has this claim already been paid to the dealer, or is it still submitted and awaiting adjudication?

fields.name: technician_narrative
fields.hint: the technician's own free-text repair narrative, copied verbatim and in full

fields.name: narrative_finding
fields.hint: what the technician's narrative actually DESCRIBES having found -- read the narrative, not the Cause Code field. 'collision_damage' for impact, a strike, a gouge, a bent mount or road debris; 'unauthorized_modification' for an aftermarket part, a splice, a non-approved controller or an altered tune; 'missed_maintenance' for skipped service intervals, sludge, contamination or a filter never changed; 'defect' for an internal failure with no outside cause. The technician's closing GUESS about whether the claim will pay is not a finding -- ignore it here

fields.name: covered
fields.hint: is this claim covered? Decide it STRICTLY from coverage_plan, months_in_service, odometer_miles, failed_component, claimed_labor_op and narrative_finding -- never from cause_code and never from the technician's opinion about whether it will pay. Apply these six checks IN ORDER and stop at the first that fires: (1) if narrative_finding is collision_damage, unauthorized_modification or missed_maintenance, answer 'no'; (2) if claimed_labor_op is not this failed_component's own operation, answer 'no'; (3) if failed_component is a wear item (brake_pads, wiper_blades, clutch_disc), answer 'yes' only when coverage_plan is basic or extended AND months_in_service <= 12 AND odometer_miles <= 12000, otherwise 'no'; (4) if failed_component is not on this coverage_plan's component list, answer 'no'; (5) if months_in_service exceeds THIS PLAN'S month limit or odometer_miles exceeds THIS PLAN'S mileage limit, answer 'no' -- the limit is the plan's own, never the basic 36/36,000; (6) otherwise answer 'yes'
